summary: The three novel financial commands (export balances, accounts reconcile, payees profile) bypass the client's 5-minute response cache on their live fetches, and accounts reconcile documents that its discrepancy-candidate search is limited to YNAB's default one-year transaction lookback.
reason: All three commands are declared `pp:data-source live` (remote-only, current-state reads) but originally called the generic c.GetWithHeaders, which transparently serves a cached response up to 5 minutes old — so a user who just made a YNAB change and immediately ran export/reconcile/profile could silently see pre-change numbers with no indication of staleness. Separately, accounts reconcile compares the account's real all-time cleared_balance but only searches the last year of transactions for candidate culprits when --since-date is omitted, so an older discrepancy-causing transaction is silently absent while unrelated recent transactions are presented as the closest match. Both flagged by Greptile PR #1725 review (confidence 3/5, Issues 2 and 3).
validated_outcome: Switched the four c.GetWithHeaders call sites in these three files to c.GetWithHeadersNoCache (drop-in signature, still writes fresh responses to cache for other readers, just skips serving a stale one). Added a conditional clause to accounts reconcile's result.Note explaining the one-year lookback when --since-date is unset. Verified live: reconcile's note now reads correctly against the real API; go build/vet/test and verify (78/79, same pre-existing unrelated finding) all clean.
